Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:  
  • 2-day history of central lower abdominal (“lower tummy”) pain with mild nausea, feeling hot/sweaty, ↑ urinary frequency, and pink-tinged urine.  
  • No prior similar episodes.  

- Relevant family medical history:  
  • Mother – early-stage breast cancer (treated).  
  • Other family history not recorded.  

- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):  
  • No regular prescription or OTC medicines.  
  • Recent prescription: empiric oral antibiotic course (name/dose not documented) to be taken twice daily for 3 days.  
  • Past contraceptive implant removed 1 year ago.  
  • Drug allergy: amoxicillin (reaction details not documented).  

- Immunisation status reviewed: Not recorded.  

- Sexual and reproductive health:  
  • Regular menstrual cycles.  
  • No inter-menstrual or post-coital bleeding.  
  • No abnormal vaginal discharge.

  • Pregnancy status not recorded.

- Mammogram (if eligible): Not recorded.  
- Other pathology (e.g., HbA1c, iron studies, Vitamin D): Not recorded.  

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings: 25-54 y woman (exact age not stated) with 2-day suprapubic pain, urinary frequency, visible hematuria, low-grade temperature (37 °C), and mild nausea. No dysuria, flank pain, vaginal discharge, or systemic illness.

Most likely diagnosis: Acute uncomplicated cystitis. Supported by suprapubic pain, frequency, hematuria, female sex, and minimal systemic features.

Differentials:  
• Urolithiasis – possible given hematuria and abdominal discomfort, but pain not colicky and frequency favors cystitis.  
• Early appendicitis – low likelihood; urinary symptoms not explained and pain has not localized.

No red-flag features for pyelonephritis (no fever >38 °C, no loin pain) or ectopic pregnancy (no missed period, negative pregnancy test not recorded).

Management Plan

• Empiric oral antibiotics for presumed uncomplicated UTI – prescribed twice daily for 3 days (specific agent and dose not documented; ensure non-penicillin choice due to amoxicillin allergy).  
• Safety-net advice: seek review if pain worsens, develops back/flank pain, fever, new symptoms, or no improvement.  
• Face-to-face assessment arranged if deterioration or recurrence.  
• Pharmacy nomination confirmed for electronic prescription.  
• Recommended adequate hydration; consider OTC analgesia if required (not documented).  
• Advised to contact clinician with any concerns; no further questions from patient.

Consider:

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits): Not recorded.  
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral: Not recorded.  
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support): Not recorded.  
- CTG registration: Not recorded.  
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test): Not recorded.  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):

1. Acute uncomplicated cystitis – High likelihood: classic presentation with suprapubic pain, frequency, gross hematuria, minimal systemic signs.  
2. Urolithiasis – Moderate likelihood: hematuria and abdominal discomfort; lack of severe colicky pain or flank radiation makes less likely.  
3. Early appendicitis – Low-moderate likelihood: mid-abdominal pain and mild nausea possible; urinary findings argue against.

Quality checks

● Missing but clinically expected elements: vital signs (BP, HR), abdominal and pelvic examination findings, BMI, urinalysis, pregnancy test, immunisation review, smoking/alcohol screening detail beyond quantity, mental health screening.  
● No documented contradictions between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality: generally clear; occasional audio gaps but did not impact key clinical information.
